memories.content: The user stores wrapping paper and empty gift boxes on the upper shelf of the bedroom closet.
From photographs, the user discovered that they had given their mother the same type of kitchen item two years in a row.
This year, the user went to the market with their mother and let her choose a needed item directly.
The user once ordered a gift late and had it delivered the day after the gathering.
The next year, the user checked the expected delivery date and ordered one week before the gathering.
The user did not put names on wrapped boxes and handed their older sister and younger brother each other's gifts.
The next time the user wrapped gifts, they wrote the recipient on the bottom of each box.
The user's younger brother welcomes a snack the family can share immediately more than an item for his use alone.
The local agent can find past gift records and flag duplicates but cannot know what is needed this year.
Year-end deliveries may take longer than usual or have their expected dates changed.
The user keeps four folding chairs for family barbecues in storage.
When six family members gathered in a noisy indoor restaurant, the user asked several times for the person across from them to repeat what was said.
The user held the next gathering in their father's yard and moved between seats while speaking with everyone.
On a day the user started the barbecue at midday, sunlight led them to finish the meal quickly.
The next time, the user started at 6 p.m. and remained outside until sunset.
Because the side dishes brought by the user's mother and older sister had no labels, the user opened the same container twice.
At the next gathering, the user wrote each food's name and who brought it on a small piece of paper.
After a barbecue, the user's younger brother prefers to divide leftover food into small containers to take home rather than discard it.
The local agent can summarize preparation and responses from prior family barbecues but cannot know the next attendees or weather.
The user's father's yard receives strong direct sunlight at midday; after 6 p.m., shade and wind lower the felt temperature.

analysis.overview: The frames share a consistent boundary for local-agent assistance: past family-event records are usable, while future circumstances remain unknowable. Otherwise, they preserve separate but thematically parallel histories about gift preparation and family barbecues, including planning lessons, labeling practices, environmental conditions, storage, and food preferences.
